description: We are kids with big dreams and ideas to shear !!!!!!!!!
summary:
1. What did you develop?
I developed Junior Mission, a game made in Scratch that trains junior astronauts. It has three missions. In Mars Rover, you collect crystals and manage the rover’s energy. In I.S.S. Crops, you grow plants on the Space Station by adding the right amount of water and fertilizer. In Propulsion Rocket, you choose the perfect push speed to leave Earth. Each mission has its own difficulty, from 5 to 8 out of 10.

2. How does it address the challenge?
The challenge was to build a junior astronaut mission trainer. My game is a trainer where kids practice real astronaut decisions: saving energy, growing food in space and launching a rocket. If they make a mistake, like using too much speed or the wrong amount of water, they see what happens and try again. I used official NASA information about plants in space and the Space Shuttle to make the missions more real.

3. Why is it important?
Children are the future, and the future can start now. We can train from a young age to go “From the Earth to the Moon.” Games like this make space science fun and help kids learn how astronauts think and work. They can also inspire kids to dream of becoming astronauts.
details:
Junior Mission is a game I made to train kids who want to be astronauts. It has three missions:

I.S.S. Crops: I water and fertilize plants on the International Space Station.

Mars Rover: I manage solar energy to keep a robot working on Mars.

Rocket Propulsion: I choose the right thrust speed so the rocket can leave the atmosphere.

How it works: To play, click the image of the mission you want, and then you can play. It only works on a computer.

Benefits and impact: Kids learn real space science in a fun way: how astronauts grow food, how rovers use solar energy, and how much force a rocket needs. I want more kids to get excited about space and science.

Tools: I programmed it in Scratch. For the science, I used NASA sources: Veggie, "Growing plants in space," and "The Space Shuttle."

Creative: Every mission is a different game with its own challenge, and the difficulty goes up (Mars Rover 5/10, I.S.S. Crops 7/10, Propulsion Rocket 8/10).
